_comment: Normative constants for the Robotensor one-demonstration in-context imitation learning competition, as run by icil-orchestrator. Versions 1 to 6 were the ICIL-LiberoGen-bench validator's contracts (4 was published and rolled back); those numbers are retired and never reused. Version 7 is the first contract of the orchestrator: one track on a benchmark in its own distribution, and submissions that are runnable policy code rather than weights for a fixed architecture. Bumping spec_version changes every derived duel id.

franka_1arm.title: One-arm Franka, one demonstration
franka_1arm.blurb: The policy is shown one demonstration of a task done with one arm of a dual Franka Panda - the frames, the action trajectory and the proprioception - and must do the task from the identical initial scene.
franka_1arm._comment: Same Scene with the action trajectory: the demonstration starts in the very scene the rollout is scored in, so replaying its actions can solve the episode. That is accepted for this competition and said on the dashboard; it is not a bug when a replay policy wins. Prompts are materialized once per duel, before either side runs, and published with the event by sha256, because a demonstration of the scored scene is the answer for it. The embodiment is a dual Franka Panda driven through its full 16-D interface; the tasks need one arm.

robotwin._comment: Pinned by distribution, version and wheel sha256 once the wheel is built (robotensor/ICIL-robotwin-benchmark#86). Entry-point discovery imports code into the orchestrator, so the pin is checked from the installed distribution's metadata before anything is imported from it. null means not yet pinned, and `icil-orchestrator benchmarks check` says so.

_benchmarks_comment: Every benchmark is a separate distribution found through the `icil.benchmarks` entry point group. The orchestrator ships none: what it can score is exactly what is plugged into it.

franka_pick_and_place.title: Pick and place (one Franka arm)
franka_pick_and_place.blurb: Grasp one object and place it somewhere, with one arm. The policy is shown one demonstration - frames, the action trajectory and proprioception - and is then scored from the identical initial scene. RoboTwin 2.0's own expert produces the demonstration at evaluation time and its own check decides the outcome.

environment._comment: `embodiment` is RoboTwin's [left arm, right arm, arm distance]; the distance is fixed with the franka_1arm suite. `cameras` are the views a clip shows side by side; the cameras a policy observes are the benchmark's `info()`. A policy declares one of `action_types` on hello and returns actions of the matching dimension.

franka_stacking.title: Stacking (one Franka arm)
franka_stacking.blurb: Put one object on another and leave it standing, with one arm. The policy is shown one demonstration - frames, the action trajectory and proprioception - and is then scored from the identical initial scene. RoboTwin 2.0's own expert produces the demonstration at evaluation time and its own check decides the outcome.

franka_press_push.blurb: Reach and actuate rather than carry, with one arm. The policy is shown one demonstration - frames, the action trajectory and proprioception - and is then scored from the identical initial scene. RoboTwin 2.0's own expert produces the demonstration at evaluation time and its own check decides the outcome.

A policy declares one of `action_types` on hello and returns actions of the matching dimension.

_skills_comment: The skills are the three categories of the benchmark's surveyed `franka_1arm` suite (robotwin_icil/tasks.yml and docs/results/survey-franka-1arm.json in robotensor/ICIL-robotwin-benchmark at 98a7ffd): pick_and_place is place_empty_cup, stacking is stack_bowls_two, press_push is click_bell and press_stapler. The survey was small, 6 tasks x 3 seeds on a dual Franka, keeping a task whose expert solved at least 2 of 3 seeds with one arm. Stacking has no one-arm task, so stack_bowls_two, whose expert may switch arms, stands in: a scene the survey did not see can still make its expert use both arms. Changing the list, the ids or the codes is a spec_version bump. `max_steps` are per-skill caps; each task carries its own smaller limit from RoboTwin.

duel._crown_comment: Both sides run the identical unit list on identical prompt bytes. Per-skill success rate is stored as a fraction in [0, 1]; the final score is the mean over skills. The challenger takes the crown iff challenger.average >= king.average + score_margin / 100. Void units are excluded from both sides, and the duel is void when the void fraction exceeds max_void_fraction. Paired per-unit outcomes are published as a diagnostic and never decide the crown.
duel._sizes_comment: A RoboTwin unit is a scene build, an expert demonstration and a rollout, so a smoke duel is one unit per skill. A track may override sizes, score_margin or max_void_fraction; an override declares the same size names.

derivation.unit_id: <skills.<skill>.code>-<index over the track's units, three digits>

budgets._comment: Wall clocks the orchestrator enforces. A unit or materialization past its wall clock is void, not a loss. policy_budget_seconds is how long a policy may take over one unit, starting it and every call to it together; what it leaves of unit_wall_seconds is the benchmark's, and a policy that runs out of it loses the unit. The numbers are placeholders until the first smoke duel on the franka_1arm suite is measured.

base_image.name: icil-policy-base
base_image._comment: Placeholder until docker/policy-base is built and referenced by digest. A submission's image is built FROM exactly this digest, and the event records it.

submission._comment: A submission is a Hugging Face repository at a resolved commit sha holding `icil.yaml`, its policy code and weights. There is no architecture or model-type check: it is held to the manifest, the policy protocol and this sandbox. Its code runs only inside its own container, with no network, a read-only root filesystem, a non-root user and these limits; the orchestrator never imports, unpickles or executes anything from it. Each `tmpfs` path is a tmpfs of at most `tmpfs_bytes`, counted against `memory_bytes`, mounted nosuid and nodev, and executable when `tmpfs_exec` is true, so a policy may compile code at run time (torch.compile, Triton, C extensions) into its caches there; the first is its home and its caches' root.

media._comment: Clips are written by the benchmark's commands (demonstration.mp4 and evaluation.mp4) and stored content-addressed by sha256; the orchestrator does not encode video.

store._layout_comment: manifest.json; tracks/{track}/{head.json,queue.json,index-NNNN.jsonl}; events/{track}/{event_id}.json; media/{sha[:2]}/{sha}.mp4. Index lines are '<canonical_json>\t<ed25519_signature_hex>', append-only.

baselines._comment: The throne opens empty: the first entrant is crowned by genesis.
